name: Winter ordeal: shards and flakes
look: Winter ordeal, the winter shadow of heaven: a xianxia art where a cultivator turns winter into night: the whole night sky above the enemy cracks like a pane of black glass, and its pieces fall as black snow. Every flake is not ice but a small shard of the sky's own shadow, the colour of night, with only a thin cold violet-white edge where starlight catches it; caught in a palm it cuts and hurts. In the cracks of the sky an eye seems about to open. The snow screams as it falls, faster and denser. The mood is silent, cold and final: black on black, a few cold glints, no warm colour and no white snow at all.
subject: black snow

parts.name: SHARD
parts.text: one shard of the pane alone: an angular sliver of night, black-violet, with a one-pixel cold violet-white edge on its top side
forms: a large triangular shard as it breaks off the pane
a small six-pointed black flake, seen flat
the flake turned edge-on as it spins
falling fast, a short dark streak with a pale tip
breaking into three black specks as it lands

parts.name: FLAKE
parts.text: one black six-pointed flake of night with a thin violet-white edge, seen from several angles as it spins

parts.name: HEADING
parts.text: one long angular shard of night with a violet-white top edge, at several headings as it falls
forms: pointing down and to the right
pointing up and to the right, tumbling
pointing down and to the left

rows.name: SPIN
rows.caption: a flake falls
rows.text: one black flake falls from the top of the cell to the bottom, spinning through the angles of the FLAKE row, with a faint short trail
notes: near the bottom, a short streak

rules: The snow is black, the colour of night, with only a thin cold violet-white edge: never white snow, never a warm colour.
The figure is the enemy: the pane hangs above it, the eye looks down at it and the snow falls on it. Do not draw the figure.
Keep the colours of the second image's palette: no outline in black, no gradients wider than a few pixels.
